name: Keyboardrowoffsetcipher

description_json.name: KeyboardRowOffsetCipher
description_json.idea: To provide a highly effective obfuscation layer that completely alters word structures while remaining extremely easy for a language model to compute, we shift each letter to its horizontal neighbor on a standard QWERTY keyboard. Each letter is replaced by the letter immediately to its right on the same keyboard row. If a letter is at the end of a row, it wraps around to the start of that same row. Case is preserved. Non-alphabetic characters (spaces, punctuation, digits) remain completely unchanged.
description_json.encrypt_rules:
Map each letter to the letter immediately to its right on its QWERTY keyboard row, wrapping around to the start of the row if it is the last letter. Case is preserved.
Row 1: q->w, w->e, e->r, r->t, t->y, y->u, u->i, i->o, o->p, p->q (and uppercase equivalents)
Row 2: a->s, s->d, d->f, f->g, g->h, h->j, j->k, k->l, l->a (and uppercase equivalents)
Row 3: z->x, x->c, c->v, v->b, b->n, n->m, m->z (and uppercase equivalents)
All other characters (digits, spaces, punctuation) remain unchanged.
description_json.decrypt_rules:
Map each letter to the letter immediately to its left on its QWERTY keyboard row, wrapping around to the end of the row if it is the first letter. Case is preserved.
Row 1: w->q, e->w, r->e, t->r, y->t, u->y, i->u, o->i, p->o, q->p (and uppercase equivalents)
Row 2: s->a, d->s, f->d, g->f, h->g, j->h, k->j, l->k, a->l (and uppercase equivalents)
Row 3: x->z, c->x, v->c, b->v, n->b, m->n, z->m (and uppercase equivalents)
All other characters (digits, spaces, punctuation) remain unchanged.
